newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NAPOLI LOOKING FOR A "10 LIRE MARADONA".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NAPOLI LOOKING FOR A "10 LIRE MARADONA".

text.p: Napoli boss Corrado Ferlaino, marking the 10th anniversary of his club's first Italian league title in 1987, said on Thursday that there would be little chance of signing a player like Maradona nowadays.
"I have so much nostalgia for those days because I know it will be difficult to repeat them," he told the Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper.
"Today the league standings reflect a club's economic values more than technical ones.
"The present-day Napoli cannot allow itself to go crazy. In other times we would have chased Ronaldo, as we did with Maradona," Ferlaino said.

The Argentine joined Napoli from Barcelona in 1984 and helped Napoli to the only two titles of their history. The club has since hit financial trouble, narrowly avoiding failure several times in recent years.
Italian clubs, notably Lazio, have been chasing Barcelona's current star, Brazilian striker Ronaldo.
Ferlaino said that for Napoli, this season's domestic cup finalists, to be truly competitive another Maradona was required. "I'm looking for one who costs 10 lire," he joked.
